title: Openness, boundedness and separation of the multidegree-zero locus
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:C\to S$ be a stable unpointed genus-$g$ family, $g\geq2$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose the relative Picard sheaf $P=\operatorname{Pic}_{C/S}$ [sk-def-picard-pic] is represented by a group algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $D(T)\subseteq P(T)$ consist of classes whose restriction to each irreducible component of every geometric fibre $C_{\bar t}$ has degree zero. A class can be represented fppf locally on $T$ by an invertible module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module]; its degree on a component $Z$ is $\chi(\widetilde Z,\nu_Z^*L)-\chi(\widetilde Z,\mathcal O_{\widetilde Z})$, where $\nu_Z:\widetilde Z\to C_{\bar t}$ is the normalization of that reduced component [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], and $\chi$ is the alternating sum of the dimensions of coherent cohomology [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. This condition is independent of the local representative. The subfunctor $D\subseteq P$ is represented by an open subgroup algebraic space, and $D\to S$ is quasi-compact and separated.

proof.text: The stable-family definition makes $f$ flat, finitely presented and projective in the projective-bundle convention, with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric fibres. Projective-bundle properness makes $f$ proper. The universal global-sections theorem gives an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_T$-modules $(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{C_T}\simeq\mathcal O_T$ for every $T\to S$. The canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{C_T}$ is then an isomorphism: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$ the $R$-algebra $B=\Gamma(C_{\operatorname{Spec}R},\mathcal O)$ is free of rank one with a basis $e$; writing $1=ce$ and $e^2=de$ gives $e=ce^2=cde$, hence $cd=1$, so $c$ is a unit and $r\mapsto r\cdot1=rce$ is bijective. Thus the relative-curve Picard theorem applies: $P$ is smooth, locally finitely presented and quasi-separated, with representable immersion diagonal. These conclusions concern the same fppf Picard sheaf as the item.

Degrees do not depend on the fppf-local line-bundle representative: two representatives become isomorphic after a further fppf refinement, and twisting by a line from the base restricts to a trivial line on every geometric fibre. Degree is unchanged by field extension. The normalized components of a nodal curve are smooth proper curves, so their field extensions remain normal and give the normalized geometric components. Tensor additivity gives $\deg_Z(L\otimes M)=\deg_ZL+\deg_ZM$, $\deg_Z\mathcal O=0$ and $\deg_ZL^\vee=-\deg_ZL$. Thus the fibrewise condition is stable under pullback and fppf descent and defines a subgroup sheaf $D\subset P$. The normalization $\nu_Z:\widetilde Z\to Z$ of a reduced component is finite by the completed normalization model and an isomorphism over a dense open, so it is a dominant map of proper curves with function-field degree $1$; the pullback-degree theorem with $d=1$ identifies normalized-component degrees with degrees on the reduced components; the component-sum formula gives the total degree as their sum.

Work locally on $S$ on a Noetherian affine open. The structure line on an affine scheme is ample directly from the definition: the section $1$ has the whole affine scheme as its nonvanishing open. Projective-bundle projectivity becomes a closed embedding in finite projective space there; let $H=\mathcal O_C(1)$. On each fibre the very-ample-implies-ample theorem makes $H$ ample. Its normalized component degrees $h_Z$ are positive by the fibre-degree ampleness criterion. Local constancy of the Euler characteristics of $H$ and $\mathcal O_C$ permits a further open restriction with constant total degree $h$. The component-sum formula, with weights one on the reduced fibres, and the pullback-degree theorem with $d=1$ for each finite birational $\widetilde Z\to Z$ give $h=\sum_Zh_Z$, hence $0<h_Z\leq h$ on every geometric fibre. Set $N=h+1$. For any fppf-local representative $L$ on $C_T$, tensor additivity shows that the two lines $H_T\otimes L^{\otimes N}$ and $H_T\otimes L^{\otimes(-N)}$ have component degrees $h_Z+N d_Z$ and $h_Z-N d_Z$. Both are positive exactly when $d_Z=0$: if $d_Z\ne0$, one is at most $h_Z-N<0$. Consequently, by the fibre-degree ampleness criterion on each geometric fibre $C_{\bar t}$, the desired subset of $T$ is precisely the set of $t$ at which both lines are ample on the geometric fibre $C_{\bar t}$. The relative-ample-locus theorem, applied to the proper morphism $C_T\to T$ (a scheme, hence an algebraic space) and to each of the two lines, gives an open $A\subseteq T$ whose points are exactly the $t$ with the line ample on $C_{\bar t}$, with formation commuting with base change. The desired subset is the intersection of the two opens, on arbitrary test schemes $T$.

proof.text: Take a scheme presentation of $P$, refined fppf locally so that its Picard sections have line-bundle representatives. Step 3 gives an open subscheme of that presentation representing the inverse image of $D$. Step 2 makes $D$ a sub-fppf-sheaf of $P$. The open-subfunctor descent theorem now gives, for every $T\to P$, an open subscheme representing $T\times_PD$, independent of the chosen representatives. An open subfunctor of an algebraic space is an algebraic space. The tensor and inverse operations already preserve $D$, so it is an open subgroup algebraic space.

proof.text: Keep a Noetherian affine base with the embedding and constant $h$ of step 3, and put $m=2g+1$, $d=mh$. The parameter theorem supplies a finite-type scheme $V_d$ of degree-$d$ divisors in the relative smooth locus and its universal divisor $E$. The line $\mathcal O(E)\otimes H^{-m}$ defines a morphism $a:V_d\to P$: the divisor line commutes with pullback, and then one passes to the Picard sheaf. Let $W=V_d\times_PD$, an open subscheme by step 4. Since $V_d$ is finite type over a Noetherian base, it is Noetherian, and so is $W$; in particular $W$ is quasi-compact. Every geometric point of $D$ lifts to $W$: over its algebraically closed field its class has a line-bundle representative, and the uniform smooth-divisor theorem supplies $E$ of degree $mh$ with $L\otimes H^m\simeq\mathcal O(E)$. Thus $W\to D$ is surjective on field-valued point classes. The algebraic space $D$, regarded as a fibred category with discrete fibres, is a Deligne--Mumford stack (its diagonal is representable by schemes, it has an etale scheme atlas, and fppf sheaves are etale sheaves), and the quasi-compact scheme $W$ maps onto it; criterion (4)$\Rightarrow$(2) of the quasi-compact atlas theorem makes $D$ over this affine base quasi-compact. For any affine $T$ over the affine base, $W\times T\to D\times T$ is still surjective with quasi-compact source, so $D\times T$ is quasi-compact by the same criterion. Such affine neighbourhoods cover $S$ and an affine test over $S$ is covered by finitely many affine opens over them, proving $D\to S$ quasi-compact.

proof.text: For a geometric fibre and a multidegree-zero line $M$, a nonzero section pulls back to sections on all normalized components. On any component where it is nonzero, degree zero and the section-degree positivity theorem make it nowhere zero. Its values at every nodal branch on that component are then nonzero. In the completed nodal local model the two branch residues of a section agree after a local trivialization of $M$. Thus the nonzero residue forces the neighbouring component section to be nonzero as well. The component graph is connected (otherwise its two unions of components would disconnect the curve), so every component section is nowhere zero. Faithful local completion, or just equality of the common residue at the node, shows that the original section is nowhere zero and trivializes $M$. Conversely a trivial line has a nonzero section; the universal structure-sheaf theorem on this proper connected reduced fibre gives $h^0(\mathcal O)=1$. Therefore $M\simeq\mathcal O$ if and only if $h^0(M)\geq1$.

proof.text: The diagonal of $D/S$ is a representable immersion: it is the restriction of the immersion diagonal of $P/S$ from step 1. Indeed base change preserves its open-then-closed factorization by the two immersion base-change lemmas. Test it over any scheme chart $T\to D\times_SD$, and refine $T$ by an fppf covering on which the difference of the two Picard sections is represented by a line $M$ on $C_T$. Every geometric fibre of $M$ has multidegree zero. By step 6 the set-theoretic image of the pulled-back diagonal is exactly $\{t:h^0(C_{\bar t},M_{\bar t})\geq1\}$. Flat base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ gives $\dim_{\kappa(t)}H^0(C_t,M_t)=\dim_\Omega H^0(C_{\bar t},M_{\bar t})$, so this is the set where the $\kappa(t)$-fibre has $h^0\geq1$. Upper semicontinuity makes this closed: $C_T\to T$ is proper and finitely presented and $M$ is finitely presented and flat over $T$, since it is invertible on the flat family. No reducedness of $T$ is required for upper semicontinuity. The flat-locally-finitely-presented openness theorem makes each member of the fppf covering an open map. The complement of the diagonal image in $T$ is therefore the union of the open images of these local complements, and is open. The original immersion over $T$ has closed image, hence is a closed immersion by the immersion-with-closed-image criterion. This holds for every scheme test, so the diagonal of $D/S$ is closed, proving separatedness.
